properties.name: loop_status's 12.1s median is three measured AMPLIFIERS over a 1.29s baseline — and 32 of 39 calls were automation firing in duplicate pairs, not the agent
properties.statement:
THE FIRST USAGE LEDGER (v0.59.0, 150 timed calls, 2026-09-12) SAYS loop_status IS 71.4% OF ALL TIME SPENT IN REFLOW2: n=38, median 12,089 ms, min 4,692, max 52,393, total 604 s of 846 s. Anthony's unmeasured estimate of "one takes 12.5s" was accurate.

THE BASELINE IS NOT THE PROBLEM. Same store, same release binary, measured in isolation: warm 1,284 ms, cold 3,309 ms. A PHYSICAL COPY of the live store profiles identically (warm 1,299 ms), so neither graph size (4,343 nodes / 25,004 edges) nor RocksDB compaction debt (19 SSTs / 25 MB live vs 5 SSTs / 14 MB rebuilt) is the cause.

FOUR HYPOTHESES FALSIFIED BY MEASUREMENT, in order:
  1. Debug binary — refuted: `ps` shows the live server IS target/release.
  2. Shared-daemon transport — refuted by A/B on one store: stdio 1,222 ms vs shared 1,214 ms, 1.0x.
  3. Store physical layout / compaction debt — refuted: physical copy of the live store, 1,299 ms warm.
  4. The instrument is wrong — refuted: a live call bracketed by an independent clock was stamped 1,291 ms by the ledger and agreed. The ledger's `ms` is sound.

THREE AMPLIFIERS, EACH MEASURED, over the 1,284 ms baseline:
  A. A WRITE BEFORE THE CALL: x3.2 (1,291 -> 4,096 ms steady, live config). The derived-scan memo is keyed per write generation (dec:derived-scans-are-memoised-per-write-generation), so a session that is WORKING never holds it. This is the dominant code-side factor and the fixable one.
  B. CONCURRENT CALLERS: x1.6 at four clients (3,148 -> 5,184 ms each, cold path). Sublinear, so not the main term.
  C. MACHINE LOAD: up to x6. sar for the day: the 52,393 ms pair sits at ldavg 6.35-8.49 with 12 blocked (a cargo release build); the same call is 8,127 ms at ldavg 0.02 and 1,291 ms at ldavg 0.12.
  `--export-to` costs nothing measurable (1,291 vs 1,299 ms) and was ruled out.

THE FREQUENCY FINDING, AND IT MAY MATTER MORE THAN THE LATENCY. 32 of 39 loop_status calls came from client `rmcp`, only 7 from `claude-code`. 14 instants carry TWO loop_status calls at the same second, from two different seats, with durations within 1% of each other (10:54:50 8,041/8,055; 12:20:42 52,255/52,393). So roughly 80% of the 604 s is spent on rollups the agent never asked for, and half of those are exact concurrent duplicates. The ledger also shows 54 distinct seats across 150 calls.

CONSEQUENCE FOR PRIORITISATION: ranking tools by measured cost puts loop_status first by a factor of ten over everything else (record_change 62.5 s, export_graph 62.1 s, all others under 40 s). But its cost is not earned by the agent leaning on it — it is a hook firing it twice per stop, in the one state (post-write) where its memo cannot help.

NOT ESTABLISHED: which process the `rmcp` client is (the Stop-hook path in tools/loop_nudge.py is the leading candidate, unverified); whether the duplicate pair is one caller racing itself or two distinct callers; whether the 1,284 ms baseline can reach the under-1-second target Anthony asked for without attacking open_defects' intrinsic ~5 s, which was left unstarted on 2026-09-05 pending his ruling. No fix has been made and no budget has been rewritten.

BOUNDS: one machine (4 cores), release build, live store and a physical copy of it, stdio and shared transports, medians of 3-4 runs, load 0.1-0.4 during the controlled runs. Instruments: tools/agent_surface_profile.py plus four purpose-built harnesses in the session scratchpad.
